description: Exercises draft-pidlisnyi-aps-03 section 2.4's requirement that a resolver select the key version authorized at a delegation's issued_at, not the key current at verification time. Same identifier and verification_method throughout; K1 is authorized for issued_at before rotation_boundary, K2 for issued_at at or after it. Every vector is verified at now, which is after rotation_boundary, so every vector exercises resolution across the rotation, not resolution before it happened.

historical.name: historical-key-resolution
historical.description: Resolves the key authorized at the delegation's own issued_at against rotation_boundary. This is the correct draft-03 section 2.4 behavior and is the fixture's positive control.

current_key_only.name: current-key-only
current_key_only.description: Negative control. Ignores issued_at and always resolves to the key that is current at verification time (K2, since every vector here is verified after rotation_boundary). This is exactly the insufficient behavior draft-03 section 2.4 names: 'selecting the key that is current at verification time is insufficient.'

cases.description: issued_at before rotation_boundary, signed with K1, verified after rotation_boundary. K1 is the key authorized at issued_at, so this is valid. A verifier that instead resolves the key current at verification time (K2) fails this vector, which is what current-key-only does.
issued_at after rotation_boundary, signed with K2. K2 is the key authorized at issued_at, so this is valid.

issued_at after rotation_boundary, but the signature was actually produced with K1, the retired key. A resolver correctly picks K2 for this issued_at, so K2's public key is checked against a signature K1 produced, and the signature check fails. K1 is not authorized at this issued_at.

issued_at before rotation_boundary, but the signature was actually produced with K2, a key not yet authorized then. A resolver correctly picks K1 for this issued_at, so K1's public key is checked against a signature K2 produced, and the signature check fails.

issued_at one second before rotation_boundary, signed with K1, same key/time relationship as KRH-01 but adjacent to the boundary. The vector's profile records that no timestamp or transparency-log evidence anchors this issued_at claim against the boundary. Per draft-03 section 2.4's second paragraph, when key retirement makes the result depend on whether an artifact was signed before a boundary and no acceptable timestamp or log evidence is identified, the key-authority result is indeterminate, even when the signature is cryptographically valid. See README 'Known SDK gap'.
cases.known_sdk_gap_reason: resolveVerificationKey / resolve_verification_key in both reference SDKs is called with (issuer, verification_method, issued_at) only. Neither SDK's key-resolution surface carries a timestamp-evidence or transparency-log input, and neither treats a boundary-adjacent issued_at differently from one with a wide margin. Both SDKs resolve this vector identically to KRH-01 and return valid, not indeterminate.
